cells.tense: You sit with people from a read that lands whole, and it holds.
cells.ask: Name one thing you notice about someone close to you, and say it to them today, plainly.
cells.core:
A face, a room, a moment — the read lands whole, before reasoning catches up. You don't argue yourself into it, and you don't need the whole picture for it to be of use. When an answer isn't there yet, the question can stay open, and the conversation can keep going around it.

People feel that. They bring you the thing they're circling, because near you the loose parts settle and the missing ones stop vanishing. That steadiness is what this is for — it keeps other people steady. Say one of the small true things out loud today, so what settles has somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: You read what matters before you can explain why.
cells.verb: seeing what deserves attention before you can say how you see it
cells.place: in the space between people, where one being meets another

cells.tense: You will have every angle covered before you will let the room have you.
cells.ask: Bring one unfinished thing to someone, say it plainly, and leave it unfinished with them.
cells.core:
Going well here looks like this: the read comes early, you say it while it's still rough, and the person across from you gets to meet you instead of your summary. You can be half-wrong and stay in the room after — that is what keeps the read useful instead of airtight. The other person gets an opening to disagree, correct you, or add what they see.

What happens instead is the gathering. More angles, more sources, one more look before it's allowed to stand. The collection gets thorough enough that the person meets a wall where you meant to meet them. One unfinished sentence, said now, does what the pile cannot.

cells.tense: You used to have the read cold, and now you want the room to confirm it.
cells.ask: Ask two people what they see in your situation, then write one line of what actually rings true.
cells.core:
Going well here looks like trusting the first version long enough to act — the read arrives, you take one step, and the picture sharpens as you move. That is this working when it's fed: in the open, one step at a time, not waiting for the whole frame to be delivered.

What happens instead is the checking. What does the other person think, what would a friend do, which answer sounds most like the one that would hold. The replies come back and none of them lands the way the first one would have. Sit with one question this week without forcing it to resolve. The first step that comes is enough to take.

cells.tense: Your best calls arrive already made, and you file them under timing or luck.
cells.ask: Pick one recent decision that felt random, and write the moment the call was actually made.
cells.core:
Going well here looks like acting without ceremony — you meet someone and something about the situation is clear before the talk is halfway done, and you move on it. People leave steadier than they came and you'd say they loosened up on their own. That is the work happening with no announcement attached to it.

What happens instead is the receipt going missing. You chose the room, the person, the thing to leave alone — the act happened, the name on it didn't. Notice one moment this week where the read led and write it down as yours. The calls are no less true for being yours.

attempts.check: The one claim the record cannot prove is that any given person's knowing has actually proved right, or that a past room ever taught them to doubt themselves; I describe the pattern only as the record frames it, and never state what happened or who did it. A reader could reasonably say they never wanted more, that confusion never touched them, or that nothing was ever disowned — which is why the ask is built as something visible and optional, not conditional on my read being correct. Each ask survives being wrong because it is worth doing anyway. The sentence that serves me more than them is the neat phrase 'the veil becomes a wall' — I keep that out of the cell and let the plain description stand.
